newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 petro products demand seen at 81 mln t.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 petro products demand seen at 81 mln t.

text.p: India's demand for petroleum products in 1996/97 (April-March) is forecast at 81 million tonnes against 74 million in 1995/96, a senior government official said on Friday.

Devi Dayal, additional secretary in the Petroleum Ministry, told a petroleum technology conference that India's imports of crude in 1996/97 were likely to be around 30 million tonnes against 27 million in 1995/96.
"We have estimated the domestic demand for petroleum products by 2001/02 at 115 million tonnes and by 2006/07 at 155 million tonnes," Dayal said.

He said India's oil pool deficit -- which is the amount reimbursed by the government to oil companies to make up for subsidised prices -- is expected to be 155 billion rupees in 1996/97. The deficit was pegged at 57 billion rupees in 1995/96.
